title: Stroke: history or residual deficits
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's past stroke and any residual deficits.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for post-stroke mobility.

HPI: Copied forward from prior visit: Patient is a 78-year-old male who experienced a cerebral infarction approximately two years ago. He presents for evaluation of lingering motor deficits. He remains left-hand dominant and continues to utilize his left side for most daily activities. He reports stable mobility but notes some fatigue during long walks.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on RA, Temp 98.6F.

Medication List:
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily
- Aspirin 81mg daily

Review of Systems:
- Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, weight change.
- Neurological: Positive for left-sided hemiparesis. Negative for headache or dizziness.
- Musculoskeletal: Negative for joint pain.

Exam:
The patient is alert and oriented. He is left-handed. Physical examination reveals persistent left-sided hemiparesis. Strength is 4/5 in the left upper and lower extremities. No new neurological findings.

Assessment:
1. Residual left-sided hemiparesis following a past ischemic stroke.

Plan:
1. Continue current medications as prescribed.
2. Physical therapy and occupational therapy to maintain current mobility and function.
3. Return to clinic in 3 months for routine follow-up.

Electronically signed,
R. Mensah, NP
May 14, 2026
explanations: Residual hemiparesis after an ischemic stroke, left dominant side: I69.352 (HCC 253).

distractors.why: Check the documented handedness; when it is not documented, the right side is dominant and the left side non-dominant.
Residual hemiparesis is documented: code the sequela (I69.35-, HCC 253), not Z86.73.
